basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurologic dysfunction is common (>30%). Hepatic and ocular damage vary across PEX16 phenotypes; qualifying frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic injury is not established in >=30% across the PEX16 spectrum, which includes milder neurologic phenotypes.
decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment or progressive neurologic dysfunction occurs commonly (>30%) across the spectrum.
decisions.ocular: none: damaging retinal or other ocular disease is not established in >=30% across PEX16 phenotypes.

basis: Severe thyrotoxicosis; heart failure occurs in roughly 40%, and encephalopathy is a major diagnostic feature. Tachycardia alone does not qualify.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: acute cardiac decompensation, including heart failure in roughly 40%, represents direct organ dysfunction during the storm.
decisions.neurologic: involved: toxic encephalopathy, delirium or impaired consciousness is a major diagnostic feature and represents cerebral dysfunction.

basis: Diffuse lymphatic malformation; destructive bone lesions occur in ~75%, pleuropulmonary involvement in ~50%, and splenic lymphatic infiltration in roughly half.

decisions.haematologic: involved: splenic lymphatic lesions occupy and replace splenic tissue in roughly half of patients; this is direct structural involvement.

basis: Deep extremity soft-tissue sarcoma; lung metastases directly occupy pulmonary tissue in roughly 50-70% over the course. Brain and bone metastases are less common.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary metastases occur in roughly 50-70% over the usual course and constitute direct occupation by the same malignancy.

basis: Protein deficiency with defining skin/hair abnormalities and hepatic fatty infiltration, necrosis or fibrosis; both organ manifestations appear in the disease's own definition.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic fatty infiltration and associated liver injury are explicitly part of the disease definition.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: nutritional skin and hair abnormalities are defining features, also reflected in the supplied synonyms.

basis: Primary brain-development disorder; renal agenesis/reflux is annotated frequent (30-79%). Short stature and unspecified cortical bone morphology do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent abnormal cortical bone morphology and short stature do not establish destructive lesions or impaired skeletal function.

basis: Skin/hair hypopigmentation and neurologic impairment define GS1; retinopathy occurs in 80-99%. Hyperlipidemia is a separately diagnosed metabolic condition; immunodeficiency is absent.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hyperlipidemia, although annotated in 30-79%, is a separately diagnosed metabolic condition rather than direct endocrine organ damage.

basis: Leukoencephalopathy with defining deafness (7/7); anemia occurs in 3/7 (~43%). Renal insufficiency in 2/7 is borderline and omitted; lactate elevation alone adds no axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: lactate elevation in 4/8 and isolated respiratory-chain findings do not establish a defining metabolic disorder or common endocrine damage.
decisions.otologic: primary: deafness is an explicitly named disease manifestation, supported by congenital sensorineural hearing impairment in 7/7.

basis: Ketogenesis/leucine defect; hepatic injury in 14/20 (70%), developmental delay in 17/35 (~49%), and anemia/coagulation abnormalities annotated frequent (30-79%).

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia is annotated frequent (30-79%), supported by frequent coagulation abnormalities; these are manifestations of metabolic decompensation.

basis: Malignancy arising from vascular endothelium in scalp skin. Lung spread is possible, but the supplied evidence does not establish involvement in >=30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the tumour originates in vascular endothelium, directly involving cutaneous blood vessels; capillaries are included in this axis.
